sections.title: A local clipboard workspace for Windows & Android.
sections.lede: Capture, organize, look back through history, lock what's sensitive, and export — all on your own machine.

items.title: Capture anything you copy
items.body: Text, code, URLs, and images land in a searchable local SQLite database. The inspector shows each clip's character count and SHA-256 digest.

items.title: Time Machine history
items.body: Every clip stays on an append-only timeline. Step back through a work session, jump to any day from a calendar heatmap, and recall older clips without losing anything copied since.

items.title: Vault Lock for sensitive clips
items.body: Choose which items to encrypt at rest — passwords, tokens, secrets — with AES-256-GCM. Keys come from an 8+ character passphrase via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations, per NIST SP 800-63B), and an interrupted lock or unlock recovers cleanly.

items.title: Settings in the main window
items.body: Hotkeys, database maintenance, and the three included themes (Vault Noir, Slate Gray, Archive Heritage) live inside the app window, not a separate dialog.

items.title: Quick Paste
items.body: Pull up your clip history from any app with a global hotkey and paste without leaving the window you're working in.

items.title: A standalone Android vault
items.body: Save text, links, and photos on the phone itself, no cloud required. Edit notes, sort them into Safes, and make encrypted offline backups (AES-256-GCM) of vaults up to 64 MiB.

items.title: Safes, Favorites, and cleanup
items.body: Group clips into named Safes, pin the ones you use daily, and review cleanup suggestions that find duplicates.

items.title: Exports with receipts
items.body: Export selected content as a portable folder or ZIP with a readable index (index.html), machine-readable manifest (manifest.json), and stamped receipt (stamped_receipt.txt).

items.title: What data is captured by Cache Vault?
items.body: Text snippets, developer code, URLs, and image buffers copied to your system clipboard while Cache Vault is active.

items.title: How does Time Machine history work?
items.body: A normal clipboard overwrites itself. Time Machine keeps every clip on an append-only timeline instead, so you can step back through earlier work sessions, jump to a specific day from a heatmap, and recall older clips without losing anything copied since.

items.title: How does Vault Lock protect sensitive data at rest?
items.body: When Vault Lock is enabled, sensitive items (such as passwords, tokens, API keys, and connection strings) are selectively encrypted using AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption. Encryption keys are derived via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) from an 8+ character passphrase complying with NIST SP 800-63B standards (4-digit PINs are rate-limited UI locks only). Transitions are guarded by an atomic SQLite transition journal with FULL sync durability.

items.title: Do the Windows desktop and Android mobile apps require each other?
items.body: No. Both apps are completely independent, full-featured local vaults. The Windows app stores clips in a local SQLite WAL database. The Android app stores text, links, and photos directly in an on-device SQLite database. If you wish to send items between them, you can optionally pair them over your local Wi-Fi network using TLS with certificate pinning (TOFU), without any cloud server.

items.title: Is my clipboard data uploaded to the cloud?
items.body: No cloud account or cloud storage is required. Core desktop and mobile features work 100% locally on your machines. Optional companion communication is peer-to-peer over your local network.

items.title: How does offline encrypted backup work on Android?
items.body: The Android app provides native AES-256-GCM encrypted backup directly to device storage. Backups are encrypted under a user passphrase before writing to disk, and staged via bounded memory streams to protect device performance even for phone-local vaults up to 64 MiB with 10 MiB assets.
